newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Proposed Romatex sale still on - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Proposed Romatex sale still on - chairman.

text.p: The proposed sale of Romatex Ltd to Consolidated Frame Textiles Ltd (Confram) would go ahead subject to the Competition Board's approval, said Brian Connellan, chairman of Romatex.
"If the Competition Board approves it (the sale) the deal will be on," Connellan told Reuters on Thursday.
"It is out of our hands now. We have indicated to the Competition Board that we would like a speedy answer on this," he said.
Connellan was responding to market speculation on Thursday that the planned sale by C.G. Smith Ltd of its 60 percent stake in Romatex to Confram could be off.

Shares in Romatex dived 40 percent to a low of 330 cents on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Thursday in response to a cautionary announcement which said any bid for the textile company would be at less than 330 cents a share.

Connellan said C.G. Smith and Romatex, who jointly put out the cautionary, had felt it necessary to quell speculation about the planned deal which had seen Romatex's share price surge earlier this week.
"There has been so much speculation that we felt it was ethically prudent...to again caution shareholders," he said.
Analysts expressed surprise at the bid price of less than 330 cents, saying a price of between seven and eight rand had been seen as a reasonable price to pay for a Romatex share.

Asked whether the bid price was not very low, Connellan said: "Maybe C.G. Smith knows more about the business than analysts do." He added that the price was set by the market on the day the transaction was looked at.
The cautionary announcement said 330 cents was the price ruling on the JSE at the close of business last Friday.
Connellan said approval from the JSE and the Securities Regulation Panel for the deal was expected to be received this week.
Romatex shares were last trading at 375 cents, down 175 cents or 32 percent, but off their worst levels of the day.
